research_question.title: Fixed-curve five-term relation compiler with rank and descent
research_question.motivation: The recursive expansion experiments measured support and first-witness lookup, but not a relation matrix, factor-base logarithm recovery, or individual target descent. The fixed-curve preprocessing lead is only meaningful when advice, preprocessing, online work, target yield, rank, and descent are charged in one end-to-end workflow.
research_question.decision_target: Decide whether a witness-bearing four-sum advice table for a coordinate factor base can support a complete toy five-term index-calculus workflow and improve the matched-random fixed-curve preprocessing diagnostic without hiding relation, rank, or descent costs.

field_types: prime fields selected independently of p-1 smoothness and constrained to p mod 4 = 3
curve_families: generated nonsingular ordinary non-anomalous non-special-j prime-order short-Weierstrass curves
methods: five-term target decomposition by scanning one factor-base point
mod-q rank and factor-base logarithm solve
matched Pollard-rho and random factor-base controls

constraints: The compiler may inspect curve coordinates and perform group and field arithmetic, but may not use factor-base discrete logarithms.
Offline construction, advice bits and bytes, logical lookup traffic, relation collection, linear algebra, and individual descent are reported separately.
All relation right-hand sides arise from explicitly charged known multiples of the fixed generator.
Exact five-term support is measured on the complete toy group; it is not inferred from a random-sum heuristic.
Coordinate families are compared with independently seeded random-x and random-scalar controls at equal cardinality and on the same curves and target schedule.
The scalar-progression control is ineligible for promotion because its construction discloses factor-base logarithms and is intended only to test the compression-versus-coverage tradeoff.
A functional toy solve is not an exponent improvement or a deployment-relevant break.
